content.title: About
content.content: Cereal, O's, flavored are crunchy corn rings coated with a sweet flavored glaze. The product is designed for a quick breakfast and is ready by simply adding milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The rings are made from whole corn that undergoes an extrusion process.
The flavored coating typically contains sugar, flavorings, and sometimes added vitamins.
The O's brand was first launched in the 1990s and quickly became popular with children.
The product is often marketed as a "30‑second breakfast".
Packaging usually contains a 30‑40 g serving, convenient for on‑the‑go consumption.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The cereal provides a fast‑acting source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Fortified with vitamins
items.content: Many versions are enriched with B‑vitamins and iron to support metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many snack foods, the cereal contains little fat.

items.title: Convenient preparation
items.content: It only requires adding milk or yogurt, saving time in the morning.

items.title: Supports satiety
items.content: The crunchy texture can help maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sugary coating can raise blood glucose levels, so consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn, experiencing skin or digestive reactions.

items.title: Low fiber
items.content: Compared with whole‑grain cereals, this product provides little dietary fiber.

items.title: Artificial flavorings
items.content: Certain versions may contain artificial flavorings that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The rings can be eaten dry as a snack, added to milk, yogurt, or kefir. They are also used in desserts, sprinkled over ice cream or fruit salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. For extended shelf life, keep in the refrigerator to preserve crunchiness.

content.title: About
content.content: Flavored latte is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from espresso, milk, and natural flavorings (vanilla, caramel, nut, etc.). It combines the strength of coffee with the smooth creaminess of milk and adds a taste note that makes the drink more versatile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Latte originated in Italy; the word “latte” means “milk”.
Flavored versions appeared in the US in the 1970s as part of the specialty coffee movement.
A typical latte contains 60‑100 mg of caffeine per serving, depending on the espresso dose.
Natural extracts are often used for flavor, though artificial flavorings are also common.
Latte is usually served in large cups (300‑350 ml), making it popular in offices.

items.title: Energizing effect
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, improving focus and reducing fatigue.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine may boost metabolic rate and aid calorie burning.

items.title: Calcium from milk
items.content: The milk component provides calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee supplies small amounts of B2, B3, and B5 vitamins involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after caffeine.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Flavored lattes often contain added sugar, increasing their calorie count.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should choose dairy‑free alternatives or use plant‑based milks.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can raise stomach acidity, causing heartburn in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: To prepare a latte, combine one shot of espresso with hot milk in a 1:3 ratio, add the chosen flavoring and, if desired, a sweetener. It is best enjoyed within 30‑60 minutes of preparation while the aroma and temperature are optimal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared flavored latte should be refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours. Prolonged storage can diminish flavor intensity and milk freshness. Gently reheat before drinking, but avoid boiling.

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen Mocha Coffee Drink is a refreshing cold beverage that blends aromatic espresso, rich chocolate syrup, and creamy milk. Served as a frozen cocktail, often topped with whipped cream and a dusting of cocoa powder.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink combines coffee and chocolate flavors, making it popular among dessert‑coffee lovers.
The frozen version lets you enjoy coffee in hot weather without the heat.
Cold espresso is usually used to prevent flavor dilution during freezing.
Some recipes add ice cream or protein powder for a thicker texture.
Frozen Mocha is often served in glass cups with a straw, garnished with chocolate shavings.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Both coffee and cocoa contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Espresso provides a quick energy lift thanks to caffeine.

items.title: Mood support
items.content: Caffeine and theobromine in chocolate can improve mood and alertness.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D (when made with milk)
items.content: Dairy components supply calcium and vitamin D, important for bone health.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: A frozen drink encourages fluid intake during warm weather.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: High caffeine intake may cause anxiety, insomnia, and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Chocolate syrup and added sweeteners increase calories and can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: If made with cow's milk, people with lactose intolerance should use alternatives.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: Rare, but possible allergic reactions to coffee components.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the Frozen Mocha Coffee Drink immediately after preparation while it remains cold and slightly slushy. Top with whipped cream, sprinkle cocoa powder, or add chocolate shavings. For extra creaminess, stir in a scoop of ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared drink in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight container, noting that the texture may change after thawing.

green-beans-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked.title: Green beans canned, reduced sodium, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green beans with reduced sodium are cooked in butter or margarine. The beans retain a crisp texture and characteristic flavor, while the added fat enhances aroma and makes the dish more satisfying.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned beans are a convenient ingredient for quick meals because they are ready to eat straight from the can.
Reduced sodium helps lower salt intake without sacrificing taste.
Cooking in butter or margarine gives a richer flavor compared with beans canned in water.
Green beans are a good source of plant protein and fiber, making them a healthy addition to the diet.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt content helps maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beans provide vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They contain iron, magnesium and potassium, which support heart and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in green beans help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beans.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking with butter or margarine adds saturated fat, so total fat intake should be considered.

items.title: BPA in cans
items.content: Older cans may contain BPA; choose products packaged in BPA‑free containers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beans can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, soups, stews, or used as a side dish for meat and fish. They can also be briefly sautéed with extra herbs and spices for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3‑4 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.

content.title: About
content.content: Pancakes are thin, round cakes made from a liquid batter of flour, milk, eggs, and a small amount of sugar. The batter cooks quickly on a hot skillet, forming a soft, lightly golden surface. Pancakes are traditionally served with sour cream, honey, jam, berries, or simply plain.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes are known worldwide: in Russia they are called “bliny”, in France “crêpes”, in Japan “okonomiyaki”.
The tradition of eating pancakes on Maslenitsa is linked to bidding farewell to winter and welcoming spring.
The largest pancake on record measured over 15 meters in diameter and was made in Russia in 2015.
Pancakes can be sweet or savory depending on batter additives and fillings.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pancakes provide a quick source of energy thanks to their carbohydrate content.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter supply a modest amount of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs are rich in B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, which support metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Milk contributes calcium and phosphorus, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional pancakes are made with wheat flour, which can be problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Pancakes can raise blood sugar quickly, so they should be consumed in moderation, especially by individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking in oil increases the fat content; using a moderate amount of vegetable oil is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pancakes can be served with sour cream, honey, jam, fresh berries, cottage cheese, caviar, or meat fillings. They are also used as a base for rolls and casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a stack separated by parchment paper and use within 1‑2 months.
